record.paper_title: The Higgs program and open questions in particle physics and cosmology
record.original_question: Are there light degrees of freedom that are singlets under the Standard Model gauge group, especially states related to dark matter, and can the Higgs sector reveal or constrain them? A concrete version asks whether adding a real scalar field S(x) in the gauge-singlet representation (1,1)_0, possibly mixing with the Higgs field or appearing in Higgs decays such as h → SS when kinematically allowed, describes new light physics accessible to Higgs measurements.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider an extension of the Standard Model obtained by adding a single real scalar field S(x) transforming in the gauge-singlet representation (1,1)_0 under the Standard Model gauge group SU(3)_C × SU(2)_L × U(1)_Y. Let H denote the Standard Model Higgs doublet, with physical Higgs mass M_h ≈ 125 GeV, and write the most general renormalizable scalar potential

  V(H, S) = μ_H^2 |H|^2 + λ_H |H|^4 + (a_1 |H|^2 S + a_2 |H|^2 S^2) + (b_1 S + b_2 S^2 + b_3 S^3 + b_4 S^4),

so that after electroweak symmetry breaking S can mix with the neutral CP-even Higgs and, if the physical singlet mass M_S satisfies M_S < M_h/2, the decay channel h → SS is kinematically open.

Address the following:

(a) Determine whether there exist light degrees of freedom that are singlets under the Standard Model gauge group — in particular, light states associated with dark matter — that mix with the Higgs sector or appear in exotic Higgs decays.

(b) Within the singlet-scalar extension above, characterize the regions of parameter space (couplings a_1, a_2, mass M_S, and Higgs–singlet mixing angle) that are compatible with current measurements of Higgs production, Higgs couplings, and direct/indirect searches for h → SS and for an additional scalar mixing with h.

(c) Identify Higgs-sector observables (signal-strength modifications, invisible or exotic Higgs branching ratios, off-shell Higgs effects, double-Higgs production) that can reveal or definitively exclude such a light singlet scalar.
artifact.status_search_result: The existence of light Standard-Model-singlet degrees of freedom (including dark-matter–related states) coupling through the Higgs portal remains an active open question. As of 2025–2026, ATLAS and CMS continue to set bounds on Higgs–singlet mixing, invisible/exotic Higgs decays, and h → SS channels, but no discovery has been made and viable parameter space remains. No theoretical proof exists ruling such states in or out.

status_evidence.title: Combination of searches for invisible decays of the Higgs boson (ATLAS)
status_evidence.snippet: Upper limit on B(h → invisible) of 0.107 at 95% CL, consistent with SM; constrains Higgs-portal singlet scalar dark matter.
status_evidence.claim: Searches continue to constrain but not exclude light SM-singlet states coupled via the Higgs.

status_evidence.title: Search for exotic decays of the Higgs boson into light scalars (CMS)
status_evidence.snippet: CMS searches for h → SS with S a light singlet-like scalar set limits on branching fractions but find no signal.
status_evidence.claim: h → SS remains experimentally unobserved with viable parameter space remaining.
